segments.arabic: [1194] حدثنا آدم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا ثابت عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Adam related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. Thabit related to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: مر النبي ﷺ بامرأة عند قبر وهي تبكي، فقال اتقي الله واصبري
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a woman at a grave while she was weeping. He said, “Fear Allah and be patient.”

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Malik:
The Prophet passed by a woman who was sitting and weeping beside a grave and said to her, "Fear Allah and be patient."

segments.arabic: [1195] حدثنا إسماعيل بن عبد الله قال: حدثني مالك عن أيوب السختياني عن محمد بن سيرين عن أم عطية الأنصارية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Isma‘il ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Umm ‘Atiyyah al-Ansariyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: دخل علينا رسول الله ﷺ حين توفيت ابنته، فقال اغسلنها ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن ذلك بماء وسدر واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا أو شيئا من كافور فإذا فرغتن فآذنني فلما فرغنا آذناه فأعطانا حقوه، فقال أشعرنها إياه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to us when his daughter died. He said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that if you see fit, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor—or some camphor—in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” When we had finished, we let him know. He gave us his waist-wrapper and said, “Place it next to her body.”

segments.arabic: تعني إزاره
segments.english: She means his waist-wrapper.

comparisons.note: The word ishar concerns an inner wrapping next to the body; the generic shroud wording does not express this distinction.

checkedBody: Narrated Um 'Atiyya al-Ansariya:

Allah's Apostle came to us when his daughter died and said, "Wash her thrice or five times or more, if you see it necessary, with water and Sidr and then apply camphor or some camphor at the end; and when you finish, notify me." So when we finished it, we informed him and he gave us his waist-sheet and told us to shroud the dead body in it.
comparisons.note: The final narrator explanation identifying the waist-wrapper is not separately retained. The instruction concerns placing the wrapper next to the body. No layer count is supplied by the selected wording.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.

Keep the conditional, camphor alternative, gave verb, notification and final attributed waist-wrapper explanation. The wrapping instruction means placing the garment next to the body; no layer count is inserted.

segments.arabic: [1196] حدثنا محمد حدثنا عبد الوهاب الثقفي عن أيوب عن محمد عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Muhammad related to us. ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: دخل علينا رسول الله ﷺ ونحن نغسل ابنته، فقال اغسلنها ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك بماء وسدر واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا فإذا فرغتن فآذنني فلما فرغنا آذناه فألقى إلينا حقوه، فقال أشعرنها إياه،
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to us while we were washing his daughter. He said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” When we had finished, we let him know. He cast his waist-wrapper to us and said, “Place it next to her body.”

segments.arabic: فقال أيوب وحدثتني حفصة بمثل حديث محمد وكان في حديث حفصة اغسلنها وترا وكان فيه ثلاثا أو خمسا أو سبعا وكان فيه أنه قال ابدؤوا بميامنها ومواضع الوضوء منها وكان فيه أن أم عطية قالت ومشطناها ثلاثة قرون
segments.english: Ayyub said: Hafsah also related to me the like of Muhammad’s hadith. Hafsah’s hadith included: “Wash her an odd number of times.” It included: “Three or five or seven.” It included that he said: “Begin with her right side and her places of ablution.” It included that Umm ‘Atiyyah said: “We combed her hair into three braids.”

comparisons.note: Supplies a conditional clause and camphor alternative not in this selected occurrence; these cannot be copied from a parallel report. Adds an al-Ansariyyah attribution and a final waist-wrapper explanation absent from this occurrence. The selected cast-to-us action must also remain distinct.

checkedBody: Narrated Um 'Atiyya

Allah's Apostle came to us and we were giving a bath to his (dead) daughter and said, "Wash her three, five or more times with water and Sidr and sprinkle camphor on her at the end; and when you finish, notify me." So when we finished, we informed him and he gave us his waist-sheet and told us to shroud her in it. Aiyub said that Hafsa narrated to him a narration similar to that of Muhammad in which it was said that the bath was to be given for an odd number of times, and the numbers 3, 5 or 7 were mentioned. It was also said that they were to start with the right side and with the parts which were washed in ablution, and that Um 'Atiyya also mentioned, "We combed her hair and divided them in three braids."
comparisons.note: Uses gave rather than the selected cast-to-us verb and supplies a sprinkle action for camphor.

notes: Keep the complete Hafsah route and every enumerated alternative; do not standardize it using the nearby washing reports.

Do not import a conditional or some-camphor alternative from another occurrence. Retain cast, Ayyub’s Hafsah route and all four included clauses, including seven. The prior 1196-conditional intake finding was erroneous: both prints omit the conditional here. The later addendum explicitly corrects that finding without altering the historical record or Arabic.

The historical opening has related to me and informed us, where selected and modern have related to us twice. Preserve the selected reporting verbs. segments.arabic: [1199] حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن حماد أخبرنا ابن عون عن محمد عن أم عطية قالت
segments.english: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad related to us. Ibn ‘Awn informed us, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, who said:

segments.arabic: توفيت بنت النبي ﷺ، فقال لنا اغسلنها ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن فإذا فرغتن فآذنني فلما فرغنا آذناه فنزع من حقوه إزاره، وقال أشعرنها إياه
segments.english: The daughter of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died. He said to us, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that if you see fit. When you have finished, let me know.” When we had finished, we let him know. He removed his waist-wrapper from his waist and said, “Place it next to her body.”

comparisons.note: The source says he removed his waist-wrapper from his waist; do not reduce the action to undid.

checkedBody: Narrated Um 'Atiyya:

The daughter of the Prophet expired, and he said to us, "Wash her three or five times, or more if you see it necessary, and when you finish, notify me." So, (when we finished) we informed him and he unfastened his waist-sheet and told us to shroud her in it.
comparisons.note: Uses unfastened instead of the explicit removal from his waist.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.

segments.arabic: [1200] حدثنا حامد بن عمر حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن محمد عن أم عطية قالت
segments.english: Hamid ibn ‘Umar related to us. Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, who said:

segments.arabic: توفيت إحدى بنات النبي ﷺ فخرج، فقال اغسلنها ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن بماء وسدر واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا أو شيئا من كافور فإذا فرغتن فآذنني قالت فلما فرغنا آذناه فألقى إلينا حقوه، فقال أشعرنها إياه
segments.english: One of the daughters of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died. He came out and said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that if you see fit, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor—or some camphor—in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” She said: When we had finished, we let him know. He cast his waist-wrapper to us and said, “Place it next to her body.”

segments.arabic: وعن أيوب عن حفصة عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها بنحوه وقالت إنه قال اغسلنها ثلاثا أو خمسا أو سبعا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن قالت حفصة قالت أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها وجعلنا رأسها ثلاثة قرون
segments.english: And from Ayyub, from Hafsah, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, the like of it. She said that he said: “Wash her three or five or seven times, or more than that if you see fit.” Hafsah said: Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said: “We arranged the hair on her head into three braids.”

comparisons.note: The second route omits the explicit seven-times alternative retained by the selected source and both prints. The second route is introduced through Ayyub and Hafsah; retain both names, the two honorifics and seven rather than replacing the route with a generic parallel.

checkedBody: Narrated Muhammad:

Um 'Atiyya said, "One of the daughters of the Prophet died and he came out and said, 'Wash her three or five times or more, if you think it necessary, with water and Sidr, and last of all put camphor (or some camphor) and when you finish, inform me.' " Um Atiyya added, "When we finished we informed him and he gave us his waist-sheet and said, 'Shroud her in it.' " And Um 'Atiyya (in another narration) added, "The Prophet said, 'Wash her three, five or seven times or more, if you think it necessary.' " Hafsa said that Um 'Atiyya had also said, "We entwined her hair into three braids."
comparisons.note: The second Ayyub/Hafsah route is abbreviated and the selected cast-to-us verb becomes gave.

notes: One selected paragraph contains modern references 1258/1259, including the seven-times alternative and three-braids closing.

The selected occurrence includes two printed references, 1258 and 1259. Preserve both complete Ayyub routes, both companion honorifics, the seven alternative and final three-braid clause. They remain one stable selected entry.

segments.arabic: [1202] حدثنا أحمد حدثنا عبد الله بن وهب أخبرنا ابن جريج أن أيوب أخبره قال: سمعت ابن سيرين يقول
segments.english: Ahmad related to us. ‘Abdullah ibn Wahb related to us. Ibn Jurayj informed us that Ayyub informed him. He said: I heard Ibn Sirin say:

segments.arabic: جاءت أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها امرأة من الأنصار من اللاتي بايعن قدمت البصرة تبادر ابنا لها فلم تدركه فحدثتنا قالت
segments.english: Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, came—a woman of the Ansar, one of those who had pledged allegiance. She came to Basra, hastening to reach a son of hers, but she did not reach him. She related to us, saying:

segments.arabic: دخل علينا النبي ﷺ ونحن نغسل ابنته، فقال اغسلنها ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن ذلك بماء وسدر واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا فإذا فرغتن فآذنني قالت فلما فرغنا ألقى إلينا حقوه، فقال أشعرنها إياه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to us while we were washing his daughter. He said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that if you see fit, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” She said: When we had finished, he cast his waist-wrapper to us and said, “Place it next to her body.”

segments.arabic: ولم يزد على ذلك ولا أدري أي بناته وزعم أن الإشعار الففنها فيه وكذلك كان ابن سرين يأمر بالمرأة أن تشعر ولا تؤزر
segments.english: He did not add anything beyond that. I do not know which of his daughters it was. And he stated that ishar means: “Wrap her in it.” Likewise, Ibn Sirin used to instruct that a woman be wrapped in it, not have it tied around her waist.

comparisons.note: Replaces the central report with a reference to 1196; this is not a complete rendering of this occurrence. The arrival account says she hastened to reach a son and did not reach him, without explicitly saying that she could not find him. The final no-addition clause belongs to transmission discussion.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Sirin:

Um 'Atiyya (an Ansari woman who gave the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet ) came to Basra to visit her son, but she could not find him. She narrated to us, "The Prophet came to us while we were giving bath to his (dead) daughter, he said: 'Wash her three times, five times or more, if you think it necessary, with water and Sidr, and last of all put camphor, and when you finish, notify me.' " Um 'Atiyya added, "After finishing, we informed him and he gave us his waist sheet and told us to shroud her in it and did not say more than that."
comparisons.note: Omits the closing uncertainty over which daughter, the explanation of ishar and Ibn Sirin’s concluding instruction. Adds a Prophetic designation after allegiance and a notification after finishing absent from the selected occurrence; the no-addition clause is not a further Prophetic statement.

notes: Keep the full embedded report, narrator uncertainty and concluding lexical/instructional material despite English abbreviations.

Keep the arrival and failure to reach her son visible outside the expandable chain. No identity of the daughter, Prophetic allegiance designation or post-washing notification is imported. Retain all final narrator remarks; the uncertainty is attributed to Ayyub by Ibn Hajar, and the ishar discussion is outside the Prophetic quotation.

The historical print names the Prophet and honorific after the allegiance clause; these are absent here from the selected and modern wording. Selected: «من اللاتي بايعن قدمت البصرة». brill-1862 (PDF 318): «من اللاتي بايعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قدمت البصرة». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 305): «من اللاتي بايعن قدمت البصرة».

The historical embedded report names the Messenger of Allah; selected and modern name the Prophet. This is separate from the previously recorded allegiance-clause difference. Selected: «دخل علينا النبي ﷺ». brill-1862 (PDF 318): «دخل علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 305): «دخل علينا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم».

segments.arabic: [1203] حدثنا قبيصة حدثنا سفيان عن هشام عن أم الهذيل عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Qabisah related to us. Sufyan related to us, from Hisham, from Umm al-Hudhayl, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: ضفرنا شعر بنت النبي ﷺ
segments.english: We braided the hair of the daughter of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: تعني ثلاثة قرون،
segments.english: She means three braids.

segments.arabic: وقال وكيع قال سفيان ناصيتها وقرنيها
segments.english: Waki‘ said: Sufyan said: “Her forelock and her two side locks.”

comparisons.note: The selected she means explanation remains attributed, and the Waki/Sufyan closing gloss names the forelock and two side locks.

checkedBody: Narrated Um 'Atiyya:
We entwined the hair of the dead daughter of the Prophet into three braids. Waki said that Sufyan said, "One braid was entwined in front and the other two were entwined on the sides of the head."
comparisons.note: Turns the narrator’s she means explanation into the report and expands the compact forelock/two-side-locks gloss.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.
Keep the she-means gloss and Waki/Sufyan forelock/two-side-locks explanation as distinct narrator notes.

segments.arabic: [1204] حدثنا مسدد حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن هشام بن حسان قال: حدثتنا حفصة عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, who said: Hafsah related to us, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: توفيت إحدى بنات النبي ﷺ فأتانا النبي ﷺ، فقال اغسلنها بالسدر وترا ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن ذلك واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا أو شيئا من كافور فإذا فرغتن فآذنني فلما فرغنا آذناه فألقى إلينا حقوه فضفرنا شعرها ثلاثة قرون وألقيناها خلفها
segments.english: One of the daughters of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to us and said, “Wash her with lote leaves an odd number of times—three or five, or more than that if you see fit. Put camphor—or some camphor—in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” When we had finished, we let him know. He cast his waist-wrapper to us. We braided her hair into three braids and placed them behind her.

comparisons.note: The first of two Prophetic honorifics is not retained in this English body; do not add an ishar instruction absent from the selected ending.

checkedBody: Narrated Um 'Atiyya:

One of the daughters of the Prophet expired and he came to us and said, "Wash her with Sidr (water) for odd number of times, i.e. three, five or more, if you think it necessary, and in the last, put camphor or (some camphor on her), and when you finish, notify me." So when we finished we informed him. He gave his waist-sheet to us (to shroud her). We entwined the hair (of the deceased girl) in three braids and made them fall at her back.
comparisons.note: Adds water and a shrouding parenthesis and collapses two Prophetic honorific positions.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.
Preserve both Prophetic honorifics, odd count, camphor alternative, notification, cast verb and the three braids placed behind. No absent inner-wrapping command or water parenthesis is added.

segments.arabic: [1205] حدثنا محمد بن مقاتل أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. ‘Abdullah informed us. Hisham ibn ‘Urwah informed us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كفن في ثلاثة أثواب يمانية بيض سحولية من كرسف ليس فيهن قميص ولا عمامة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was shrouded in three white Yemeni Suhuli cloths of cotton. There was neither a shirt nor a turban among them.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.
Retain the complete chain, three count, white/Yemeni/Suhuli/cotton descriptions and both shirt/turban exclusions.

segments.arabic: [1206] حدثنا أبو النعمان حدثنا حماد عن أيوب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهم قال
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, who said:

segments.arabic: بينما رجل واقف بعرفة إذ وقع عن راحلته فوقصته أو قال: فأوقصته قال النبي ﷺ اغسلوه بماء وسدر وكفنوه في ثوبين ولا تحنطوه ولا تخمروا رأسه فإنه يبعث يوم القيامة ملبيا
segments.english: While a man was standing at ‘Arafah, he fell from his mount and it broke his neck—or he said, caused his neck to break. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

comparisons.note: Changes the prohibition on covering the head into a prohibition on shaving it. The selected Arabic and both inspected prints have the covering verb. Omits the narrator’s alternative waqasat/awqasat wording.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

While a man was riding (his Mount) in 'Arafat, he fell down from it (his Mount) and broke his neck (and died). The Prophet said, "Wash him with water and Sidr and shroud him in two pieces of cloth, and neither perfume him, nor cover his head, for he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection saying, 'Labbaik,' (i.e. like a pilgrim)."
comparisons.note: Changes the opening standing posture to riding and omits the narrator’s alternative wording. Supplies Labbaik and a pilgrim explanation instead of retaining the selected generic reciting-the-talbiyah expression.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.

Retain standing, both alternative word forms and the plural companion honorific. Both verbs concern a broken neck. The instruction says cover, not shave; no Labbaik quotation or pilgrim gloss is inserted.

segments.arabic: [1207] حدثنا قتيبة حدثنا حماد عن أيوب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us. Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: بينما رجل واقف مع رسول الله ﷺ بعرفة إذ وقع من راحلته فأقصعته أو قال: فأقعصته، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: اغسلوه بماء وسدر وكفنوه في ثوبين ولا تحنطوه ولا تخمروا رأسه فإن الله يبعثه يوم القيامة ملبيا
segments.english: While a man was standing with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at ‘Arafah, he fell from his mount and it crushed him—or he said, killed him on the spot. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

comparisons.note: Changes the prohibition on covering the head into a prohibition on shaving it. The selected Arabic and both inspected prints have the covering verb. Omits the Aqsa/Qaas alternative and the explicit divine subject in the resurrection clause.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

While a man was at 'Arafat (for Hajj) with Allah's Apostle the fell down from his Mount and broke his neck (and died). So Allah's Apostle said, "Wash him with water and Sidr and shroud him in two pieces of cloth and neither perfume him nor cover his head, for Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection and he will be saying 'Labbaik."
comparisons.note: Omits the alternative verbs preserved in the Arabic. Supplies a Hajj parenthesis and Labbaik; preserve the source’s explicit standing and generic reciting-the-talbiyah wording.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.

Preserve standing, both Prophetic honorifics, the dual companion honorific, both alternative verbs and Allah as the explicit subject. Aqsa‘at is rendered crushed; aq‘asat, killed on the spot. Cover is not shave.

The modern fall clause uses عن where selected and historical use من. Both are recorded; the English from does not imply an Arabic correction. Selected: «إذ وقع من راحلته». brill-1862 (PDF 319): «إذ وقع من راحلته». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 306): «إذ وقع عن راحلته».

segments.arabic: [1208] حدثنا أبو النعمان أخبرنا أبو عوانة عن أبي بشر عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهم
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Abu ‘Awanah informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them:

segments.arabic: أن رجلا وقصه بعيره ونحن مع النبي ﷺ وهو محرم، فقال النبي ﷺ اغسلوه بماء وسدر وكفنوه في ثوبين ولا تمسوه طيبا ولا تخمروا رأسه فإن الله يبعثه يوم القيامة ملبيا
segments.english: A man’s camel broke his neck while we were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he was in ihram. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not touch him with perfume, and do not cover his head, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

comparisons.note: Changes the prohibition on covering the head into a prohibition on shaving it. The selected Arabic and both inspected prints have the covering verb.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

A man was killed by his camel while we were with the Prophet and he was a Muhrim. So the Prophet said, "Wash him with water and Sidr and shroud him in two pieces of cloth and neither perfume him nor cover his head, for Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection and he will be saying 'Labbaik' . "
comparisons.note: Generalizes the explicit broken-neck verb to killed and replaces the generic talbiyah phrase with Labbaik.

notes: Exact first portion of source paragraph mwYQ; the original trailing newline stays with this entry.

Preserve the explicit camel/broken-neck action, we were with the Prophet, ihram, two Prophetic honorifics and plural companion honorific. Perfume and covering instructions and Allah as subject remain.

segments.arabic: [1209] حدثنا مسدد حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن عمرو وأيوب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهم قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from ‘Amr and Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رجل واقف مع النبي ﷺ بعرفة فوقع عن راحلته
segments.english: A man was standing with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at ‘Arafah, and he fell from his mount.

segments.arabic: قال أيوب فوقصته، وقال عمرو فأقصعته
segments.english: Ayyub said: “It broke his neck.” ‘Amr said: “It crushed him.”

segments.arabic: فمات، فقال اغسلوه بماء وسدر وكفنوه في ثوبين ولا تحنطوه ولا تخمروا رأسه فإنه يبعث يوم القيامة
segments.english: He died. He said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection.”

segments.arabic: قال أيوب يلبي، وقال عمرو ملبيا
segments.english: Ayyub said: “He recites the talbiyah.” ‘Amr said: “Reciting the talbiyah.”

comparisons.note: Changes the prohibition on covering the head into a prohibition on shaving it. The selected Arabic and both inspected prints have the covering verb.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

A man fell from his Mount and died while he was with the Prophet at 'Arafat. The Prophet said, "Wash him with water and Sidr and shroud him in two pieces of cloth and neither perfume him nor cover his head, for he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection saying, 'Labbaik'."
comparisons.note: Omits the two named Ayyub/Amr alternative verbs and their distinct closing forms. Supplies Labbaik and omits the standing posture; all named alternatives and the selected lexical expression remain.

notes: Exact second portion of mwYQ. Preserve both Ayyub/Amr alternatives; no text is inferred from the preceding occurrence.
